methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
OSH Cut, a bootstrapped robotics and manufacturing company founded by Caleb and Jacom Chamberlain, lacks sufficient narrow-stage comparables for conventional valuation triangulation. The broader robotics and manufacturing sector comprises 11 peer companies—1 public (277810.KQ) and 8 private firms including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics—yet none meet the dual criteria of matching both stage and valuation tier simultaneously.

The Peer-Median method is not applicable here. The analysis identified zero same-stage peers, zero adjacent-stage peers, and zero similar-tier comparables within the sector. While an all-sector median exists across the 11 robotics companies, applying it would conflate bootstrapped-stage companies with later-stage capital structures and revenue scales, introducing material distortion. A three-datapoint minimum threshold was not met for any filtered cohort.

Given the absence of robust triangulation via comparable valuation multiples, OSH Cut's valuation requires alternative approaches—such as discounted cash flow analysis (if revenue and growth projections are available), cost-of-capital estimation based on bootstrapped equity risk, or staged-investment scenarios. The key uncertainty is the company's current revenue, margin profile, and addressable market size relative to the named private peers. Without these inputs or sufficient stage-matched comps, a defensible valuation range cannot be established from the available data.
